hints: Notice the hill blocks the direct straight-line path, so light from the transmitter cannot be seen at the house but radio waves still arrive there.
Recall that diffraction round an obstacle is large when the wavelength $\lambda$ is large compared with the obstacle, and small when $\lambda$ is very small.
Compare the wavelengths in this item - visible light is about $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ while radio waves are metres long - and decide which wave bends over the hill more.
walkthrough: Identify the observation: the hill stops the straight-line ray for seeing, but the radio signal bends into the shadow region behind the hill to reach the house.
State the governing rule: diffraction spreading round an edge or obstacle increases as wavelength increases relative to the size of the obstacle.
Compare the two waves: visible light has $\lambda \approx 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and radio waves have $\lambda$ of order metres, so $\lambda_{radio} > \lambda_{light}$ by many orders of magnitude.
Apply the rule: radio waves diffract strongly over the hilltop into the house region, while light diffracts negligibly and continues in straight lines blocked by the hill.
This combination of longer wavelength for radio waves and more diffraction of radio waves over the hill is option C.

options.A: Light does not have a longer wavelength than radio waves, and light shows negligible spreading round the large hill.
options.B: Light does have a shorter wavelength than radio waves, but shorter wavelength means less diffraction, so light cannot bend over the hill to the house.
options.C: Radio waves have a much longer wavelength than light, so they diffract significantly over the hill and reach the house.
options.D: Radio waves do not have a shorter wavelength than light - their wavelength is much longer, which is why they diffract more.
